messages:
maria (support): Hey team — Escalation from AcmeCorp (acct: acme-778). They report p95 ~1.1s but p99 spiking to 4–6s for calls that use function/tool calling + JSON schema validation. Started after we turned on strict structured-output validation a few days ago. Customer says impact is across multiple endpoints but most visible on /v1/chat/completions and our function router.

maria (support): Repro steps from customer: curl to our API with model redwood-chat-4 and function_call + schema. They included trace id x-trace-id: trace-zz-9f2. Said they see long delays before any tokens stream back (so latency is pre-token).

maria (support): Logged snippet they attached (redacted):
```
2026-02-27T15:12:10.224Z request received id=trace-zz-9f2
2026-02-27T15:12:10.226Z auth ok
2026-02-27T15:12:10.230Z start preproc: validate_schema acct=acme-778
2026-02-27T15:12:10.683Z schema validated (dur=453ms)
2026-02-27T15:12:10.690Z tool router start (dur_unknown)
2026-02-27T15:12:11.060Z tool response (dur=370ms)
2026-02-27T15:12:14.450Z token stream start (latency_pre_token=4226ms)
```

josh (eng-runtime): Thanks Maria. Can you drop the raw request body (sanitized) + headers they used? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maria (support): Sent via DM — it's hosted, customer in eu-west1. Body includes a ~120-field JSON schema (lots of nested objects and enums) for the tool output. They pass `function_call` with name "order_lookup".

sara (eng-ml): Pinging in. From high-level telemetry for that trace id: model latency (GPU token generation) is normal. The pre-token stall looks entirely in the request pipeline: JSON schema validation and tool_router serial calls. We have a couple of histograms that correlate: `json_schema_validation_ms` and `tool_router_latency_ms`. For that timeframe json_schema_validation_ms p99 ~480ms and tool_router_latency_ms p99 ~520ms for requests with structured-output enabled.

sara (eng-ml): Quick profiler snippet (aggregated samples):
```
- request_pipeline: 70%
  - json_validator.validate: 35% (avg=220ms, p99=480ms)
  - tool_router.resolve_and_call: 28% (avg=175ms, p99=520ms)
  - io/other: 7%
- model.generate: 30%
```

josh (eng-runtime): That matches an internal experiment we ran — large schemas blow up sync validation cost, and our router currently validates each tool candidate synchronously before routing (safe but expensive). Two quick asks: can you attach a minimal repro we can run here? Also what SDK/client are they using?

maria (support): They used our JS SDK v0.9.4 (server side). Minimal repro attached in DM; I'll paste sanitized version: 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, X-Region: eu-west1, X-Trace-Id: trace-zz-9f2
Body: {
  "model": "redwood-chat-4",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"get order 12345"}],
  "function_call": { "name": "order_lookup" },
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "order_lookup",
      "parameters": { /* ~120 props nested */ }
    }
  ],
  "stream": false
}
```

alan (eng-sre): For immediate mitigation we can flip a feature-flag to disable strict structured-output validation for that customer (bypass and fall back to best-effort post-hoc validation). That will be non-breaking for APIs that still want function calling; we need product approval. Can we get a quick risk assessment?

kevin (product): If we bypass validation we must flag customer's API responses as "unvalidated" in the response metadata and add a short grace period. I'd be okay with a temporary bypass for an SLA-hit customer. Need eng to confirm how fast we can toggle.

josh (eng-runtime): Technical mitigation options (short list):
- Bypass strict validation per-account (feature flag) — fastest (minutes to hours with rollout/QA).
- Compile schemas into a fast validator on first use and cache compiled validators per-account + SHA key (reduces repeated compile cost).
- Offload validation to async/background with streaming: start streaming tokens and validate incrementally as data emits (requires changes to streaming pipeline).
- Change router to parallel validation of tool candidates and short-circuit when first valid match found (trades CPU for latency).
- Increase concurrency/workers on tool router for hosted eu-west1 (capacity tweak).

sara (eng-ml): Addendum — some schemas include heavy `oneOf` combinator usage which is worst-case for many validators. Compiling transforms those into fast codepaths and helps; naive re-validation each request is the big cost. Also tool router currently does a sync call to each tool adapter (auth + cold adapter init) before returning; we can short-circuit on a match but that requires router changes.

maria (support): Customer is asking for a near-term ETA — they're losing revenue. Can we prioritize a patch?

josh (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate steps: 1) Alan flips per-account bypass for acme-778 (emergency config) 2) Deploy a compiled-validator cache patch to canary (single line change to use `compiled_schema_cache.get_or_compile(schema_sha)`) — low risk, should cut p99 validation by ~3–5x for repeated schemas. 3) Add metrics for `tool_router_attempts` and `tool_router_parallel_ms` for visibility. I can put up a PR for (2) today; need SRE help for (1).

alan (eng-sre): I can flip bypass for acme-778 now in the runtime config store. Will monitor. Also will scale tool-router pod count by +20% in eu-west1 as a temporary capacity measure. Deploying in 5m.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: redwood-runtime v3.14.2-hotfix -> eu-west1 (owner: josh)

sara (eng-ml): If we do the compiled-schema caching we should also add an eviction policy keyed by account + schema-sha because private deployments might not want global cache sharing. Keep it account-scoped.

josh (eng-runtime): Agree. Also add a fast-path that when stream=true we skip full-structure validation pre-stream and perform incremental validation (will need careful rollback but can be gated behind a flag).

maria (support): Alan — customer confirmed they'll accept bypass if it improves p99 now. Please confirm when flipped and I'll relay.

alan (eng-sre): Bypass flipped for acme-778 at 15:34:22 UTC. Also scaled tool-router pods +20%. Monitoring logs.

maria (support): Customer reports immediate improvement: p99 down from ~4.8s to ~650ms within 90s. They said some requests still slow but much better. :tada:

josh (eng-runtime): PR opened for compiled-schema cache: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/8123 — contains tests + feature-flag. Plan: canary -> eu-west1 -> global if stable.

deploy-bot: canary deploy complete: redwood-runtime v3.14.2-hotfix -> eu-west1 -> success (canary pass)

sara (eng-ml): Post-mortem notes to include:
- Root cause: heavy synchronous schema compilation/validation + serial tool candidate validation increased pre-token latency for structured-output flows.
- Contributing factor: large `oneOf`-style schemas from customer and router doing sync adapter handshake before routing.
- Short-term mitigations: per-account bypass + scale up + canary compiled-validator cache.
- Long-term: incremental streaming validation, parallel router, compiled-schema caching + account-scoped eviction.

kevin (product): I'll own customer comms: apology + explanation + timeline for permanent fix. Also suggest optional settings in Console to allow customers to opt for "low-latency mode" that relaxes strict pre-validation for production-critical workflows.

maria (support): Thanks everyone. I'll close the escalation once PR merges and we confirm no regression for acme. Ticket: ESC-2026-3312.

josh (eng-runtime): Leaving the thread with action items: PR#8123 (compile-cache) -> canary monitor 24h; router metrics added; product feature request for Low-Latency Mode.

alan (eng-sre): Will keep the bypass in place for 48h unless product asks to remove earlier. Adding synthetic to monitor json_schema_validation_ms and tool_router_latency_ms every minute for acme-778.

maria (support): closing note to thread: customer extremely appreciative of fast response; they asked for postmortem and preferred timeline (kevin will lead). If anything regresses ping me. :pray:
